scenes.text: In use case 1, we saw how phone call assistants work, speech to text, the AI brain, then text to speech. [1] Today, we build our own talking assistant in Python. [2] You speak, it thinks, and it talks back.

Here's the loop. [1] Record your voice from the microphone. [2] Whisper turns the speech into text. [3] The language model writes a reply. [4] A text to speech engine turns the reply into audio. [5] And the speaker plays it. Then, repeat.

You need three things. [1] Whisper, an open speech recognition model that runs on your computer. [2] A text to speech engine, like pyttsx3, which uses your computer's built-in voices. [3] And sounddevice, to record from the microphone.

[1] Here's the full assistant. [2] Import the libraries. [3] Load the Whisper model, the speech engine, and the AI client. [4] In a loop, wait for Enter, then record five seconds of audio, and save it to a file. [5] Whisper transcribes the audio into text. [6] Send the text to the model, and ask for a short, one sentence reply, because long answers are boring to listen to. [7] Finally, speak the reply out loud. [8] Try it, and have a conversation!

scenes.text: Want a nicer voice? [1] Built-in voices are free and instant, but sound robotic. [2] Neural voices, like Kokoro, which makes the voice you're hearing right now, sound much more human, and still run on your own computer.

Here are four terms for voice apps. [1] Latency, the delay before it replies. Keep it under about a second, to feel natural. [2] Streaming, speaking the first words while the rest is still being written. [3] VAD, voice activity detection, knowing when you've stopped talking. [4] And barge-in, letting you interrupt the assistant.

Here's a common belief. [1] People think voice assistants must feel slow and clunky. [2] Our simple version waits for each step. Real assistants stream every stage, and overlap them, to reply in under a second.

data.myth: Voice assistants must feel slow and clunky.
data.fact: Real assistants stream and overlap every stage to reply in under a second.
